extra_quotes: Element-specific synchrotron spectroscopies are uniquely suited to understand magnetic properties in the light of the details of the local microscopic electronic structure.

Specifically, X-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) 24–26 and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS)27,28 have provided fundamental insight into related vdW magnets 29,30, and start to be increasingly applied to exfoliated few-layer samples31 to separate dimensionality from bulk electronic structure, as in NiPS3 32.
X-ray absorption, XMCD, and RIXS spectra at the Fe L3,2 edges were simulated within the Anderson impurity model as implemented in the many-body package QUANTY 37,38.

Reaching the genuine 2D limit, however, remains challenging: flakes, produced by mechanical exfoliation, have limited lateral extension34—often smaller than the footprint of soft X-ray synchrotron beams— and relatively poor surface cleanliness.
Additionally, finding small flakes across the macroscopic surface of a substrate can be practically challenging in the experimental setups where these techniques are implemented.
